title: 1 Samuel 28
paragraphs: ¹ Around that time, the Philistines mustered their forces for war against Israel. Achish said to David, "Understand that you and your men are expected to march out with me in the army." ² David said, "Then you will see for yourself what your servant can do." Achish replied, "Good — I'll make you my personal bodyguard for life." ³ Now Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned him and buried him in Ramah, his hometown. And Saul had expelled all the mediums and spiritists from the land. ⁴ The Philistines assembled and camped at Shunem, while Saul gathered all Israel and camped at Gilboa. ⁵ When Saul saw the Philistine army, he was terrified and his heart was gripped with fear.

⁶ Saul prayed to the LORD, but the LORD did not answer him — not by dreams, not by the Urim, not through prophets. ⁷ Saul told his servants, "Find me a woman who consults the dead, so I can go and seek guidance from her." His servants said, "There is a woman at Endor who consults the dead." ⁸ Saul disguised himself, putting on different clothes, and set out at night with two men. He came to the woman and said, "Use your power to consult the dead for me. Bring up the person I name." ⁹ The woman said, "Surely you know what Saul has done — how he's expelled all the mediums and spiritists from the land. Are you setting a trap for me, trying to get me killed?" ¹⁰ Saul swore to her by the LORD, "As the LORD lives, you won't be punished for this."

¹¹ Then the woman asked, "Who shall I bring up?" He said, "Bring up Samuel." ¹² When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed loudly and said to Saul, "Why did you deceive me? You are Saul!" ¹³ The king said to her, "Don't be afraid. What do you see?" The woman said, "I see a divine figure coming up from the ground." ¹⁴ He asked, "What does he look like?" She said, "An old man is coming up, wearing a robe." Saul realized it was Samuel, and he bowed down with his face to the ground in reverence. ¹⁵ Samuel said to Saul, "Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?" Saul answered, "I'm in desperate trouble. The Philistines are attacking me, and God has turned away from me. He no longer answers me — not through prophets, not through dreams. So I've called on you to tell me what to do."

¹⁶ Samuel said, "Why do you consult me? The LORD has turned away from you and become your enemy. ¹⁷ The LORD has done exactly what he told you through me: he has torn the kingdom from your hands and given it to your neighbor David. ¹⁸ This happened because you did not obey the LORD and did not carry out his fierce judgment against the Amalekites. That is why the LORD has done this to you today. ¹⁹ The LORD will also hand Israel over to the Philistines along with you. Tomorrow you and your sons will be here with me. The LORD will hand the Israelite army over to the Philistines as well." ²⁰ Immediately Saul collapsed full length on the ground, overwhelmed with terror at Samuel's words. He had no strength left — he had eaten nothing all day and all night.

²¹ The woman came to Saul and saw that he was shaking violently. She said, "Look — your servant obeyed you. I risked my life and did what you asked me. ²² Now please listen to me in turn: let me bring you some food to eat, so you'll have strength for the journey." ²³ He refused, saying, "I won't eat." But his servants joined the woman in urging him, and he finally gave in to them. He got up from the ground and sat on the bed. ²⁴ The woman had a fattened calf at the house. She quickly slaughtered it, then took flour, kneaded it, and baked unleavened bread. ²⁵ She set it before Saul and his servants, and they ate. Then they got up and left that same night.
